name: Beat Clock
description: The song's position as ground truth: a sample-accurate mapping from audio playback position to beats and bars, with latency calibration. It exists separately from utility.timer_system because frame timers drift against the audio hardware clock — over a three-minute song that drift is multiple judgement windows, and a rhythm game whose clock slides reads as broken no matter how generous the windows are. This component owns the bpm map, the beat/bar phase, and the two latency offsets (audio output and input path) that calibration measures; it deliberately does not play audio — presentation.audio_system starts and stops the track, and this clock reads the position. It also does not react to its own beats: ui.note_highway and utility.judgement_window subscribe, and the clock stays ignorant of both, so the same clock can drive a lane game, a dance game, or a boss that attacks on the downbeat.

inputs.name: bpmMap
inputs.description: Entries of {beat, bpm} marking tempo changes. A map rather than a scalar because real charts accelerate; constant-bpm songs are a one-entry map.

inputs.name: offsetSeconds
inputs.description: Where beat zero sits in the audio. Almost no chart starts exactly at sample zero, and a wrong offset poisons every beat that follows.

inputs.name: audioLatencySeconds
inputs.description: Output-path delay: what the player hears lags the clock. Measured by calibration, not guessed — Bluetooth alone can add a fifth of a second.

inputs.name: inputLatencySeconds
inputs.description: Input-path delay: the press lags the player's intent. Combined with audio latency, this is the number judgement deltas are corrected by.

inputs.name: calibrationStepSeconds
inputs.description: Increment the calibration flow nudges offsets by. Ten milliseconds is fine enough to converge, coarse enough that manual calibration terminates.

outputs.name: beatPhase
outputs.description: 0..1 position within the current beat — the value scroll positions and pulse animations interpolate from.
